correctness.rationale: For normal N the spectral measure identity ||N^n x||^2=integral |z|^(2n) dmu_x gives bounded orbits exactly when mu_x has no mass outside |z|<=1: positive mass outside contains an annulus |z|>=1+1/k of positive mass, forcing exponential growth. On the bounded orbit subspace, dominated convergence gives norm decay exactly when E_N(unit circle)=0. Uniform decay is norm-power decay for the normal restricted contraction, equivalent to ||N P||<1 and to a spectral gap r<1; the zero-subspace case is also consistent. For A=M_z on L2(planar disk area), unit-circle mass vanishes but ||A||=1; adding circle-arclength U=M_zeta changes the boundary projection but not the closed-disk spectrum or empty point spectrum. Normality gives approximate-point spectrum equal to whole spectrum. These deductions are complete spectral-theorem arguments, not finite sampling.
risk: The term strong asymptotic expansivity is interpreted with uniform convergence for all bounded-orbit vectors staying within a fixed ball, as stated in the mathematical record; alternate definitions would need rechecking.
The strict norm gap applies to restriction on bounded-orbit spectral subspace, not the whole normal operator when spectrum outside the disk occurs.

final_claim: For bounded normal operators on complex Hilbert space, bounded-orbit vectors are exactly the spectral subspace supported in the closed unit disk, asymptotic expansivity is equivalent to zero spectral projection on the unit circle, and strong asymptotic expansivity to a uniform spectral gap below it. Normal coordinate multipliers can have identical point, approximate-point and whole spectra but different asymptotic expansivity.
limitations: Normal bounded Hilbert-space operators only, not arbitrary Banach or nonnormal cases.
The current motivating paper full text and Mazur full text were inaccessible, retaining an originality comparison risk.
No independent proof of a stronger new spectral theorem beyond the classical spectral theorem is claimed.
